newsitem.title: UK: World Bank sets longest-dated rand bond at 20 yrs.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sets longest-dated rand bond at 20 yrs.

text.p: The World Bank on Wednesday launched the longest dated Eurorand bond, a 20-year zero-coupon bond via Hambros Bank.
"Its a brave move, but I think it will work," WestMerchant syndicate manager Richard Roberts said.
"It's a balance between the length of maturity and the price of the paper which is relatively cheap," he said.
The deal, worth a nominal 2.5 billion rand, was issued at 7.45 percent of face value. There were 0.5 point fees, meaning the proceeds for the World Bank will be 173.75 million rand.
"We were delighted the World Bank were prepared to work with us," Hambros syndicate manager said.
"With the gearing effect, it is a very interesting issue."
At full fees, the notes yielded around 14.25 percent.

The deal followed the success of the recently launched debut zero-coupon bond in the rand sector. That was brought for the World Bank's private sector financing arm, the International Finance Corp (IFC).
Demand came from both retail and institutional investors in Europe and Asia, Hambros said.
Dealers away from the lead said the issue was helped by tax advantages after retirement for investors in Europe and exemptions in some countries for supranationals from inheritence tax.
The deal boosted sentiment in domestic South African bond markets, traders in Johannesburg said.
The issue prompted the benchmark R150 to hurtle lower to 14.93 percent, the day's best level, and was seen as a vote of confidence in South Africa.

Hambros, a regular underwriter in the rand Eurobond market, also underwrote the deal for the IFC in mid-February -- a 400 million rand 10-year zero-coupon bond which has subsequently been increased to 800 million rand.
"It showed us there was more interest in a zero (coupon bond) and room for even a longer-life zero with a much lower issue price," the Hambros syndicate manager said.

A zero-coupon bond pays no interest over the life of the issue but is issued at a deep discount to face value. The difference between the issue and redemption prices creates a hefty capital gain which boosts the yield to market levels.
Whilst the market waits to see how the 20-year World Bank bond goes, dealers said there were rumours of a five-year zero-coupon bond for a triple-A rated European corporate borrower.
